analysis.investment_thesis: Supertech EV is a 2022-incorporated micro-cap EV manufacturer with a negligible 0.47% ROE and no meaningful earnings history — the antithesis of a Graham investment. The low headline P/E of 8.21 is meaningless when applied to razor-thin, unproven earnings on a INR 54 Cr market cap speculation.
key_strengths: Promoter skin-in-the-game at 69.31% aligns insider interests
Headline P/E of 8.21 is not nosebleed territory
Reports positive (if tiny) earnings rather than outright losses
key_risks: ROE of 0.47% indicates earnings are effectively zero — P/E is illusory
Incorporated only in 2022 — fails the 3-5 year earnings track record test
EV 2W/E-Rickshaw is hyper-competitive (Ola, TVS, Bajaj, Ather) — no moat for a 54 Cr player
red_flags: No multi-year earnings history — fails Graham's foundational requirement
0.47% ROE suggests the company barely earns its cost of capital, let alone beats it
Zero DII holding — no institutional validation
Micro-cap + recent incorporation + hot sector = classic speculative cocktail
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my vantage point, this security fails nearly every quantitative filter I apply. A company incorporated in 2022 cannot possibly demonstrate the 3-5 years of consecutive positive earnings I demand — the most basic threshold for distinguishing an investment from a speculation. The 0.47% ROE is the decisive number here: it tells me the business is producing virtually no economic return on shareholder capital, which renders the 8.21 P/E a statistical artifact rather than a sign of value. At a 54 Cr market cap with such anemic profitability, earnings are likely in the range of a few crore — any modest business disruption wipes them out entirely.

Mr. Market is offering this at a price that appears cheap on a single ratio, but that is precisely the trap that snares inexperienced investors. The EV two-wheeler and e-rickshaw industry is crowded with far better-capitalized competitors, and a nascent manufacturer has no demonstrable earning power, no dividend record, and no balance sheet evidence provided here to suggest a margin of safety. Without current ratio, debt-to-equity, or book value data, and with the data I do have failing every test, my conclusion is firm: this is speculation dressed as investing. Avoid.
